canvas-01.description: The lower part of the first sheet of the 1920 Sayreville atlas, below the heavy line that separates it from the key map and index, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. The map shows the western end of Main Street, lettered Main (Broadway), running across the foot of the sheet, and Boehmhurst (McCarthy), a street that rises from Main Street up the left side of the part. First Street and Second Street cross Boehmhurst, and Third Street lies at the top of the part beside the heavy diagonal line that bounds it. The blocks are numbered 51, 52, 53, 101 and 102. Lots on both sides of Boehmhurst and along Main Street carry small dwellings, shown in yellow, with a few outbuildings; a small pink-shaded building with a brick or stone front stands on the south side of First Street. Mitchell is drawn south of Main Street and marked not opened. A compass rose and a note about the proposed location of a pumping station for a new water system appear in the open space east of Second Street, and a six-inch water pipe is traced beside Boehmhurst. The upper left corner of the part is cut by the heavy diagonal line and the key map above it is not part of this reading. The neighbourhood is thinly built and most of the east side of the part is blank.
notes: Boehmhurst (McCarthy) is Boehmhurst Avenue today; Main (Broadway) is Main Street; modern 1st and 2nd Street meet Boehmhurst at the same places.
Mitchell, marked not opened, has no modern counterpart in the street data used.

Printed sheet 1: key map, index and specials (not to scale for georeferencing) above a heavy line; below it a 100 ft to an inch map part of Main Street (Broadway) with Boehmhurst (McCarthy), 1st, 2nd, 3rd Streets and Mitchell. Configure only the lower part (mask below the heavy line; key map excluded).

sheet-2-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 2 is the main map, drawn at 100 feet to an inch (scale bar at the foot of the sheet) with the street grid turned about 77 degrees. It shows Main Street, printed Main (Broadway), running down from the fork at the Sayreville Hall and post office to a cluster of houses, Public Schools No. 1 and No. 2 and the Sayreville M.E. Church. Hillside Avenue and Maple Avenue (Maple) run south-west from the fork, with Fisher Avenue and Elk Lane as short side streets and Bright Lane and another lane in the south. River Lane runs north-east to the Sayre & Fisher Co. Brick Works on the east edge, which has kilns, clay storage, press room, machinery room and sheds beside the Raritan River Railroad. Blocks 11 to 18, 104 and 105 are numbered. The west edge is the heavy dividing line against part 2, and Whiteheads Lane is lettered at the foot of the sheet beside Maple Av.
notes: River Lane is River Road in OpenStreetMap; Maple Av. corresponds to Maple Street
Fit is a three point helmert with 14 m residual at the fork; low confidence

100 ft. Two parts: 1 main (Main Street (Broadway), Hillside, River Road), drawn turned (rotation about 77 deg); 2 west block (Quaid, Brookside, Seminole) west of the heavy line. Main Street is 4 to 14 m off its modern line; both parts are helmerts and low confidence.

sheet-2-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 2 is the block west of the heavy dividing line, drawn at its own rotation at 100 feet to an inch. It contains Quaid Avenue and Brookside Avenue running north to Seminole, with Oak and Hickory crossing them, and Main (Broadway) running east and west across the lower part. Most of the blocks are laid out in long narrow lots, numbered 41, 42, 43, 102, 106 to 111 and 113, with few buildings, mostly frame dwellings at the street corners. Several streets are marked Not Opened or Not Named, including Arbitrary A Pl. at the bottom. A north arrow in the upper left shows the part tilted against the rest of the sheet.
notes: Placed as a two point helmert; Main Street junctions were off by 14 m and left out

100 ft. Two parts: 1 main (Main Street (Broadway), Hillside, River Road), drawn turned (rotation about 77 deg); 2 west block (Quaid, Brookside, Seminole) west of the heavy line. Main Street is 4 to 14 m off its modern line; both parts are helmerts and low confidence.

sheet-3-1.description: The main part of sheet 3, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covering the west side of Sayreville. At the top left Canal (Doeler) and Jacobsen run north and south on either side of numbered blocks 21 and 22, closely lined with small dwellings and a row of tenements. Sandfield runs east from them across the middle of the left side, past a Roman Catholic church and school with its rectory, and a long curving road runs from it north-east around a large pond that fills the upper centre. Main (Broadway) runs from the pond's south-east shore down the page, with close-set lots and dwellings on both sides, then continues south past a church, a fire department building and a town hall to meet Dolan and Kursch near the foot of the sheet. At the bottom right, Thomas, William and John bound a block of dwellings and a row of houses along Stanton (Arb.). Dashed lines mark a six-inch water pipe diagonally across the open ground in the centre. The sheet is largely blank in the middle left, and a boxed area at the top right belongs to a separate part.
notes: Main (Broadway) is Main Street today and Kursch appears to be Kupsch Street; Dolan is Dolan Street.
Sandfield Road is not in the modern street data used and has no georeferenced junction.

100 ft. Part 1 main page (Main, Dolan, Kursch = Kupsch Street, Thomas, William; Canal/Jacobsen/Sandfield upper left without control); part 2 boxed inset top right (Hart, Dane, Smullen, Mary = Rose Street), helmert along Smullen.

sheet-3-2.description: A boxed inset at the top right of sheet 3, set off by a heavy vertical line on its left and a heavy line at its foot, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. It shows a strip of the Smullen neighbourhood. Smullen runs north and south through the box, bending south-west below Dane, with a six-inch water pipe along it. Hart crosses the top and Dane crosses the middle, each with a six-inch water pipe in the street, and Mary crosses at the foot near a short John street running south of it. Lots on the east side of Smullen and along Hart are numbered 101 to 116 and carry a few small dwellings, and blocks 117 and 118 are mostly empty. The box carries the notation No Exposure along its left edge, with sheet 4 on the other side of the heavy line, and the compass rose and a sheet number 6 at its foot show that the area continues on sheet 6.
notes: Smullen north of Hensler Lane keeps its name today; Mary east of Smullen is Rose Street on modern maps.
John Street and Rose Street meet at the foot of the box but that junction was not detected.

100 ft. Part 1 main page (Main, Dolan, Kursch = Kupsch Street, Thomas, William; Canal/Jacobsen/Sandfield upper left without control); part 2 boxed inset top right (Hart, Dane, Smullen, Mary = Rose Street), helmert along Smullen.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the centre of Sayreville along Main Street, printed Main (Broadway), and the blocks east of it, at 50 feet to an inch. Main Street runs down the west side of the sheet, with Dolan Street entering from the west at the top. On the west side are shops and public buildings in a closely built strip: a motion picture theatre in hollow tile, People's Hotel, a soda water bottling works, a barber, a community house, a bowling alley with a drug store and the Central Hotel with its stable and a dance pavilion behind it. East of Main Street lie three large blocks between Kursch, Hart, Dane and Mary Streets, divided by Thomas Street and Joseph Street, with Smullen Street on the east side. Blocks are numbered 3, 116, 119, 120 and 121 and the surrounding sheets are numbered 1, 3 and 5. Most buildings are yellow frame dwellings; hollow tile and brick buildings are pink. Hart Street is drawn at an angle across the sheet. Water pipes and hydrants are marked, with a note that they are from plans, and a Princeton library stamp covers part of the lower right corner.
notes: Kursch Street is Kupsch Street in OpenStreetMap
Main Street junctions measure 4 to 6 m from the modern line and were left out of the fit
Clausen (Classen) is printed as a double name at the bottom edge
50 ft (fit 7.99 px/ft). One part. Main Street (Broadway) left out: its four junctions carried 3.8 to 5.9 m residuals in one sense.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 shows the southern part of central Sayreville at 50 feet to an inch. Main Street, printed Main (Broadway), runs down the west side and Washington Road, lettered Amboy R'd in parentheses, crosses the foot of the sheet. Church Street and Clausen Street cross the top, and Smullen Street, French (Smullen) farther south, forms the east side with Idlewild Avenue and Little Broadway entering from sheet 6. Hensler's Lane, marked sand, runs diagonally from the south-west to Smullen Street, and Albert Street runs south from it to Washington Road. The largest feature is the Catholic Cemetery in the centre, beside the Church of Our Lady of Victory with its school in the basement and the Sisters house; the Knights of Columbus Hall (from plans) stands on Church Street. In the lower left are the Middlesex Co. Hotel and stores along Main Street and Washington Road, and in the east side are houses on blocks 123 to 127. Blocks 122 to 126 are numbered, with sheets 4, 6 and 7 around it. A Princeton library stamp sits over the scale bar.
notes: Drawn streets are skewed against their modern lines; only five junctions were found and the fit is poor
Hensler's Lane is Hensler Lane in OpenStreetMap
50 ft. One part; the drawing is skewed against the modern streets (fit 8.46 px/ft, LOO 11.6 m): low confidence.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 shows a built-up residential district of Sayreville drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The map is bounded on the north by Mary Street, on the west by Smullen Street, which is lettered French (Smullen) south of Hensler's Lane, and on the south by Washington Road, lettered Amboy Road in parentheses. Blocks 32 to 37 and 127 and 128 are laid out between John, James, Quaid and Smith Streets, with Idlewild Avenue and Little Broadway crossing them from west to east. Almost all the buildings are small yellow frame dwellings with sheds and outbuildings; a few brick or hollow tile buildings are shaded pink, among them a meat and grocery store at Quaid Street and Idlewild Avenue and a hotel on Washington Road. Lot numbers are printed along the street fronts and 6 inch water pipes with hydrants run in most streets. The lower left carries the corner of Liberty Street and the Muschick Bros. embroidery works, and the lower right shows Embroidery Street (marked 10 feet wide) and Walling Street meeting Washington Road at the edge of sheet 7. Adjoining sheets are indicated by the numbers 3, 5 and 7 in the margins. The street lettering is large and clear, and the scale bar is at the bottom right.
notes: Old Mary Street east of Smullen Street is Rose Street in OpenStreetMap
Liberty Street south of Washington Road is Cecelia Street today
Washington Road is also printed Amboy Road
Smullen Street south of Hensler's Lane is printed French (Smullen) and is French Street today
Hensler's Lane is Hensler Lane today
Pilot. Smullen/French, John, James, Quaid, Smith, Mary, Idlewild Av, Little Broadway, Washington Road; 50 ft scale (fit 7.87 px/ft) although the key map is 100 ft.

sheet-7-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 7 is the main map of the sheet at 50 feet to an inch. Washington Road, printed Washington R'd (Amboy R'd), crosses the top edge, and Liberty runs down the left side. Embroidery Street runs south through the middle, with the Muscatt Mfg Co. night gown factory on its east side, and Walling Street parallels it to the east. Conduit Street crosses the lower left. The blocks are long lots with a few frame dwellings, and the Muscatt works is drawn in pink with its fuel and fire protection noted. Blocks 6, 10, 40 and 129 are numbered.
notes: Liberty is Cecelia Street in OpenStreetMap; Conduit is not in the extract
Washington Road is cut by the top edge; points were hand-picked

50 ft. Three parts: 1 main (Embroidery, Liberty = Cecelia Street, Washington Road), anchored; 2 middle strip of lots 19 to 48 along Washington Road, unplaced; 3 bottom strip on Washington Road at Main, anchored.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: middle strip: Washington Road lots 19 to 48 (no street junction; needs step 6b carried points from sheet-7-3 (lot 48 continues as lot 49 at the left edge of part 3)).

sheet-7-3.description: Part 3 of sheet 7 is the strip along the foot of the sheet showing Washington Road, lettered Washington R'd (Amboy R'd), with lots numbered 49 to 92 along both sides, Public School No. 2 on the north side and a garage with capacity for 30 cars. The strip ends at the right with Main at the edge. Houses are frame dwellings with a few pink buildings.
notes: Placed by one hand-picked point at Main Street and Washington Road; low confidence

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 of the 1920 Sayreville atlas, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers clay and brick-making land south and west of the village along Washington Road. Washington Road, lettered Washington Rd. (Amboy Rd.), crosses the middle of the sheet from the South River on the left to the right edge. The Sayre and Fisher brick yard stands north of the road beside the South River, drawn as long yellow drying sheds and pits, with a second yard of sheds south of it, and a larger works lettered as not in operation lies south of the road with ruins of kilns and sheds. Several large ponds, the former clay pits, sit in the middle and right of the sheet. Sandfield Rd. runs diagonally from the upper left to the lower left, and another Sandfield Rd. and Jernees Mills Rd. run north and south at the right of the sheet, meeting Washington Road. A few dwellings stand near the road and at the left. A compass rose with a north arrow is at the right and a scale note reads 100 ft to an inch.
notes: Jernees Mills Road is Jernee Mill Road today; Sandfield Road has no counterpart in the modern street data used.
Only one junction (Jernee Mill Road and Washington Road) is georeferenced; the part is anchored on it with a configured scale.
100 ft. Brickworks and clay pits (Sayre and Fisher, Furman yards); one part anchored on Jernees Mills Road (Jernee Mill Road) / Washington Road.

sheet-9-1.description: The top strip of sheet 9, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, shows the built frontage of Washington Road, lettered Washington Rd. (Amboy Rd.), across the east side of Sayreville. Kathryn runs north from the road at the left among small dwellings, with blocks 138, 139, 143 and 144. East of it Ridge Av., Union Av. and Clark Av. are drawn south of the road as dashed, not-opened streets, and Union Av. or Outlook Av. runs north from it. Krumb, also not opened, and Harrison run north of the road at the right, and Pershing Av. runs south at the far right with blocks 140, 141, 142, 145, 146, 149 and 166. Most of the area is blank lots with scattered dwellings, and a six-inch water pipe follows the road. The heavy line along the foot of the strip separates it from the New York Clay Co. hollow tile works and from the central blocks of Maple, Pine and Greenhill, which are separate parts of the sheet.
notes: Control rests on three points along Washington Road only; the placement is a helmert and low confidence.
Clark Av. may correspond to modern Krumb Street by spacing along Washington Road; not verified.
A street lettered here could not be read with certainty (read as Union Avenue or Outlook Avenue); left out of the street names.

sheet-9-2.description: The lower strip of sheet 9, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, runs along Washington Road, lettered Washington Rd. (Amboy Rd.), below the heavy diagonal line that separates it from the New York Clay Co. works above. Pershing Av. runs south from the road at the left past block 152, with the Foch street crossing near the foot among small dwellings in block 153. Navisink Av. or Minnisink Av. runs south of the road near the middle, bounding block 154, and Thomas, marked not opened, closes the block on the south. Block 158 lies north of the road and 159 to the east. The buildings include a clubhouse, boarding houses, and sheds of a powder company, and a note at the foot says water pipes and hydrants are from the plans of the powder company. A scale bar reads 100 ft to one inch and the Princeton map division stamp is at the bottom. The right side of the strip carries more of the powder company grounds, with its water supply notes.
notes: Control rests on two points on Pershing Avenue (Washington Road and Foch Street); helmert and low confidence.
A street lettered here could not be read with certainty (read as Navisink Avenue or Minnisink Avenue); left out of the street names.

sheet-9-3.description: Central block of Sheet 9, enclosed by heavy lines, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that Greenhill and Woodlawn Avenues run nearly up the page. It lies south of Washington Road (Amby Road) and east of the New York Clay Company's hollow tile works, and fills a tract of company-built housing laid out by E. I. DuPont de Nemours and Company. The northern half holds blocks 163, 164, 165 and 162, two parallel streets (Greenhill and Woodlawn Avenues, each 45 feet wide) crossed by Pine Street, which is drawn only as a line of 6 inch water pipe. Small frame dwellings, mostly with porches, stand in rows along each street with house numbers marked, and a fire alarm box and several dry hydrants with hose are marked. Block 164 is labelled no exposure. South of Pine the blocks narrow into a wedge: Greenhill Avenue forks, and Maple and Deerfield Streets (both 45 feet wide) run diagonally to the south east through block 161, lined with frame dwellings numbered 1 to 20. A note states that the hydrants are supplied from the plant of E. I. DuPont de Nemours and Company. A dash-dot match line lettered A runs through the lower left corner, and lumber sheds and a large frame building lie beyond the heavy line at the left edge. A north arrow and the scale note 100 ft. to an inch appear on the east side.
notes: Printed Green Hill Av. (two words); modern Greenhill Avenue.
Pine is modern Thompson Place (water pipe line, position matches junctions with Greenhill and Woodlawn).
